title: Generated-code examination rules
rules: Compilation is necessary but not sufficient: syntactically valid padding such as item = repeated dots is a failure.
A code response must contain a complete task-shaped program, not merely an assignment or expression.
Check minimum structure, expected constructs, identifiers, control-flow relevance and output behaviour.
Check English answers for semantic relevance and minimum substantive length.
Do not continue training solely to reduce loss when proxy behaviour is collapsing or gaming the gate.
Preserve the best adapter only when proxy score, substantive code and English behaviour improve together.
summary: Promotion doctrine extracted from the stabilization run: compilation is necessary but insufficient; require task-shaped semantics, relevant control/output behavior, substantive English, and joint improvement rather than optimizing loss alone.
invariants: Loss improvement is evidence, not acceptance.
Proxy gates must resist syntactically valid padding or short-output gaming.
Preserve the best adapter only when substantive code and English behavior improve together.
